object.content:
I'm going to try and post a short summary of each day's work on Google+ when I work with electronics. I noticed that I only post final projects on my blog at http://tinkeringetc.blogspot.com/ so I wanted a way to keep people updated on my day-to-day tasks... and remind myself what I have done each day.

I received some sample parts from Texas Instruments and Maxim for the CEE (http://www.nonolithlabs.com/cee/) that I got a bare board for from their Kickstarter. I have the majority of the parts soldered on (See above post for the pictures) and soldered the Maxim op-amps on as well. The TI op-amps were in a QFN-12 package (AKA the leads are on the bottom) so I couldn't solder it on my hand. I have a hotplate that I made (http://tinkeringetc.blogspot.com/2011/06/homemade-pid-controlled-hotplate.html), but unfortunately, it is at my home now and I'm at school. I'll have to pick it up over Spring break when I return home.

I also created a new repository for my next project at https://github.com/dwaq/Homebrew-Gameboy-Cartridge . Since I just finished my MSP430 Reaction Game project (http://tinkeringetc.blogspot.com/p/msp430-reaction-game.html), I needed something else to occupy my time. Right now I only have a library that I made that contains the schematic symbols and footprints. I cannot guarantee that they are the exact size just yet as I haven't put much time into the project so far. I have made a version of a homebrew cart using a mess of wires from the idea on http://hackaday.com/2010/07/14/programmable-game-boy-cartridge-walk-through/ (pictures are two posts up), but I'd like to design a PCB too, and eventually 3D print a case for it so it appears just like a official Gameboy cartridge.
